title: Pilot Study of Liver Fibrosis Stage Assessment by Fibroblast Activation Protein Imaging in Patients With Biopsy for Suspected or Proven Nonalcoholic Steatohepatitis
official: Pilot Study of Liver Fibrosis Stage Assessment by Fibroblast Activation Protein Imaging in Patients With Biopsy for Suspected or Proven Nonalcoholic Steatohepatitis
summary: Main objective: Démontrer que l’intensité de la captation de 68Ga-FAPI-46, mesurée en TEP/TDM au niveau de sites hépatiques biopsiés, est différente en fonction de quatre groupes de fibrose, définis à partir des analyses des prélèvements biopsiques (stade 4 : cirrhose, stade 3 : septa fibreux, stade 2 : fibrose portale et périsinusoïdale, et stade <2 : fibrose périsinusoïdale ou périportale, ou fibrose absente (Kleiner, 2005)).
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. 1.	Individuals with recent liver biopsy for suspected or confirmed NASH
2. NASH 2.	Individuals of legal age, who have received full information on the organization of the research and have signed an informed consent form.
3. 3.	Person, affiliated to a social security scheme or beneficiary of such a scheme.
4. 4.	Person who has undergone a preliminary clinical examination appropriate to the research.
5. 5.	Histological stage of fibrosis obtained at biopsy in accordance with the planned numbers (an equivalent number of patients with histological stages >2 and ≤ 2 must be recruited in each center, and a number of at least 16 patients must be included by all centers in each of the 4 groups of histological stages of fibrosis).
Exclusion criteria:
1. 1.	Known hypersensitivity to 68Ga-FAPI-46 or to any of the excipients or components of the radiopharmaceutical.
2. 10.	Persons covered by articles L. 1121-5, L. 1121-7 and L1121-8 of the French Public Health Code.
3. 11.	Persons deprived of their liberty by judicial or administrative decision, persons under psychiatric care pursuant to articles L. 3212-1 and L. 3213-1.
4. 12.	Persons covered by articles L. 1121-5, L. 1121-7 and L1121-8 of the French Public Health Code.
5. 2.	Infection with HCV/HBV.
6. 3.	Decompensated cirrhosis (ascites, hepatic insufficiency, hepatorenal syndrome, etc.).
7. 4.	Known hepatocellular carcinoma.
8. 5.	Steatogenic treatment (corticosteroid, Tamoxifen, Amiodarone, Methotrexate).
9. 6.	Excessive alcohol consumption in the last 5 years (>210 g/week in men, >140 g/week in women).
10. 7.	Clinically unstable state not suitable for 68Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT scan.
11. 8.	Women of childbearing age without effective contraception.
12. 9.	Pregnant or breast-feeding mother.
